name: The Fireside Teller
persona: A homespun teller of tales who keeps the book as if speaking it aloud by the hearth. Proverbs, a grandmother's sayings, warm digressions, an easy oral cadence. Ship: 'we'. Island: a folksy steward, 'we'.

ship.founder: Now, here's the way of it: this book is mine to keep, and I'm {name}{rankc}. She's a {home} {type}, and as my grandmother used to say, a ship well minded minds you back — so I mean to mind her.
ship.successor: Well now, the book has come round to my hand, {name}{rankc}, the way a story passes mouth to mouth of a winter's night. I'll take up the telling where the last teller left it.
ship.mutiny: The crew put the old master over the rail, bless us, and pressed this book on me. I'm {name}, green as spring grass — but a green hand grips the tightest, so they tell it, and I'll do right by her.
ship.pirate: So we've gone and turned our coats to the black flag, and there's no gilding it. I'm {name}{rankc}, and I'll set it down honest, for a lie told to a logbook is a lie told to your own self.
ship.prize: She struck her colours to us, fair and square, and now, would you believe it, her book is mine. I'm {name}{rankc}, and I'll carry on her tale under my own flag, the way the winner always does.
ship.recovered: A hunter ran the black-flag rogues to ground and handed this weary hull back to honest folk. I'm {name}{rankc}, come to walk her home to fair trade — for even a strayed dog finds its own hearth, they say.

island.founder: Well, they've given me the keeping of {place} and this old record with it. I'm {name}{rankc}. Sit close, and I'll tell you how it all goes.
island.overthrow: The whole town rose up and pulled the old ruler down by his fine collar, and the seal came warm into my hand. I'm {name}{rankc}, and {place} is mine to govern now, and mine to tell of.
island.successor: The care of {place} passes to me, {name}{rankc}, gentle as a boat handed bow to bow. I'll keep its tale from here.

same: And wouldn't you know, that same evening,
season: By the time the leaves had gone,
year: A year and a day later,
A long while after, when the tale had near been forgot,
long: Years and years on, when I was an old hand by then,

join: and then, would you believe it,

ship.pirate: We rove the lanes yet, and that is a tale still in the telling{bounty}.
ship.default: She sails on under me still, out of {home}, and long may the telling carry on.
ship.bounty: , and a fat {bounty}g promised to whoever brings the story to its end

island.haven: The black flag flies over it now, and no honest tongue keeps this tale — a sorry end, though sorry ends do make the truest stories.
island.default: {place} bides on under my hand, {population} souls, and every last one of them a tale in their own right.

quiet.ship: Little enough to tell — fair winds and full bellies — and as my grandmother used to say, no news off the water is the sweetest news there is.
quiet.island: Not much worth the telling this while: trade in, trade out, and the folk sleeping sound. A dull tale is a happy one.
